_schema: Ben's review queue. Canonical store; NEEDS_REVIEW.md is the readable mirror. Entry fields: id, title, raised (ISO date), kind, status, source, what, why_it_matters, options (array, only where there is a genuine fork), recommendation, files, resolution (null until Ben answers).
_note: Companion to backlog.json and review.json, NOT a replacement for either.
PURPOSE: things awaiting BEN'S JUDGEMENT. Three kinds live here:
- 'question'        â€” an open call nobody has made yet, usually surfaced by
doing adjacent work. Not blocking, or it would be a
backlog item with blocked_on set.
- 'decision-taken'  â€” a call made ON BEN'S BEHALF so work could continue.
Recorded here so it can be OVERTURNED rather than
quietly becoming precedent. This is the important half:
an unrecorded delegated decision is indistinguishable
from a decision Ben made.
- 'observation'     â€” something noticed in passing that is too small or too
cross-cutting to file, but which a human should see.
- 'novel-work'      â€” raised by a SESSION about its own task (Ben, 2026-08-20):
the work in hand feels NOVEL â€” no owning authority doc, no
saved role or established pattern fits, or it quietly grows
the project's scope. Raise it AT THE MOMENT the feeling
arises, then continue (or pause, if scope growth is large).
Gives Ben a drift detector: novelty should be chosen, not
accreted.
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM review.json: review.json is a BLOCKER list â€” items blocked
on a visual artifact only Ben can produce (a mockup, an annotated screenshot).
Work there cannot proceed at all. Entries here are not blocking; they are
questions and reversible calls. If an entry turns out to need a mockup, move it
to review.json and leave a resolution here pointing at it.
HOW IT DIFFERS FROM backlog.json: an entry here is not work. If Ben's answer
creates work, file a backlog item and resolve the entry with that item's id.
LIFECYCLE (revised 2026-08-14, Ben's ruling): this file is TRANSIENT â€” a live
queue of open calls, not a permanent audit trail. Append entries as they arise
and set status to 'resolved' with a resolution once answered, exactly as before.
But do NOT let resolved entries accumulate: prune them promptly rather than
holding them for posterity. The reasoning is not lost â€” it lands in code
comments, an authority doc, or a backlog item's design field at the moment the
work happens, and THAT is the durable record. Ben's own framing: 'the docs
should preserve changes made, and the review queue should only be for things
of that level of importance' â€” i.e. open and unresolved, not a history of
everything ever decided. A large housekeeping sweep this date closed 231
entries down to 2 genuinely open ones on this basis.

ARCHIVAL (2026-08-23): 'prune' now means MOVE, not delete. Run node tools/session/archive_reviews.js to move every resolved entry, verbatim, into docs/development/archive/needs-review-<quarter>.json, then re-render the mirror. The hot file holds open entries only.
SEEDED 2026-08-01 at Ben's request, populated from that session.

PURGE 2026-08-23: 240 open entries -> 18. Every entry referring only to backlog ids <= BL-568 (retired by the same-day backlog purge) was retired; 16 more were answered by reading the current docs and tree. All 223 are frozen verbatim in archive/needs-review-purged-2026-08-23.json, each with a resolution saying why. The survivors are asked as a form: tools/session/register/review_queue.js, built by register/build.js, published at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/53fb4e56-2eae-439e-bcb7-121fa49bd340 . NR-576 records the calls taken in the sweep.

DRAINED 2026-09-01 on Ben's instruction, from 117 open to 0. The queue had become a shadow backlog: most entries named WORK rather than a judgement, so ten backlog items (BL-713..BL-722) were minted to carry it and every entry was closed with a resolution saying where it went. THE RULE THAT KEEPS IT DRAINED, and it is now in CLAUDE.md Rule 0c: a call only Ben can make belongs here; work belongs in backlog.json; a fact worth remembering belongs in the comment or doc next to the code.

items.title: DECISION TAKEN: how the shelf spoils (BL-1179)
items.source: the sprint 49 main session (Ben: "I'll also trust your judgement"; NR-968 brought spoilage forward)
items.what: Settled in MARKETS.md sec The shelf spoils: every good on a market shelf loses a fixed per-tick share, authored per good by class - perishable (food rations, agricultural produce, water, clean water, medical supplies) fastest, consumable (consumer goods, fuels, chemicals) slower, durable (ores, metals, alloys, materials, components) slowest but never zero; first-cut rates, then measured. Only the SHELF spoils (a corp pool is its owner's stock). Nobody is charged (the market already paid; goods leave, no credits move). Spoilage drains after the tick's draws and before the shelf's share of supply is read. The k cap stays; k > 0 is set by measurement.
items.why_it_matters: Spoilage plus the household draw are the two shelf drains that make k > 0 safe, per your 2026-10-03 ruling.
options: A: keep it
B: spoilage also bites corp pools (a holding cost)
C: one flat rate for every good
D: other

items.title: DECISION TAKEN: the lake size cap is 150 tiles (BL-1200)
items.source: the sprint 49 main session, on Ben's delegation (NR-974 said: measured)
items.what: lake_census (dff0abc1) measured 360 enclosed water bodies on the 16 curated seeds: no clean gap. The pooled dip is 89-143 tiles (3 bodies), with a dense cluster from 154 to 204 above it; 21 enclosed bodies exceed 1,000 tiles (seed 11: a 4,027-tile "lake" beside a 4,090-tile sea). Chosen: 150 - just under the cluster, keeping the near-twins 119 and 138 (seeds 25, 13) together as lakes. Pooled: 301 lakes (3,079 tiles, ~3,800 shore) and 59 seas; lakeshore falls from ~14,700 tiles to ~3,800.
items.why_it_matters: Where the line falls decides which shores give Wells free fresh water and which get ports and wharves.
options: A: keep 150
B: 100 (the pooled dip; splits seed 25s and 13s near-twins)
C: 300 (mid-size 150-300 bodies stay lakes)
D: other

items.title: DECISION TAKEN: a short shelf is shared within each phase of the tick, construction first (BL-1209)
items.source: the BL-1209 cold review
items.what: Your pro-rata ruling says every draw admitted against a short shelf in a tick shares it. The tick draws in phases: construction sites draw before labour is solved, processors after. Pooling both phases into one ration would mean reordering the tick, so the share is computed within each phase: sites share among themselves, then processors share what is left; upkeep draws stay first-come after both. A short steel shelf can therefore go to sites before plants. MARKETS.md will say so exactly.
items.why_it_matters: Construction-first can starve production of a shared input in a tight market; the alternative is a tick reorder.
options: A: keep per-phase, construction first
B: pool the phases (reorder the tick so sites and plants share one ration)
C: per-phase, production first
items.recommendation: A for sprint 49; revisit in sprint 50 (logistics) if the trade-flow lens shows sites starving plants.

items.title: DECISION TAKEN: the seat clean slate refunds everything a site was charged, not only materials (BL-1206)
items.source: the BL-1206 cold review
items.what: Your ruling read "materials paid so far refunded". The build refunds the recorded sum of every charge the site took: materials at the posted price, the flat build-cost slice, and the construction capacity it drew. A site paused for want of materials but still drawing capacity is refunded those charges too. CORPORATION_GENERATION.md step 5 now says so.
items.why_it_matters: A clean slate means the player pays for nothing they did not choose; refunding materials only would leave the flat cost of builds the AI started on the player's books.
options: A: keep - refund everything the site was charged
B: materials only (needs a field separating the flat slice and capacity)

items.title: Trade-flow lens: may "no room" reflect rivals' cargo in flight to a market?
items.source: the BL-1222 (trade-flow lens) cold review, 2026-10-07
items.what: The lens marks a short market "no room" when the destination cannot absorb more at the landed price. That room subtracts EVERY corporation's convoys in flight to it and stock pooled there, so "no room" tells the player, in aggregate, that someone is already filling that market. It names no rival and no quantity. DISCOVERY.md § Competitor visibility makes market supply/demand aggregates public but does not say whether goods in flight count. Options: (A) accept it as a public market signal (cargo on the road is observable) and say so in DISCOVERY.md; (B) compute the player's room without rivals' in-flight cargo for the lens only (a second room figure the dispatcher does not use, so the lens and the decision could disagree).

items.title: Decisions taken on your behalf building "an order is a floor, not a hold" (BL-1229)
items.source: the BL-1229 (steel stays home) build lane, 2026-10-07
items.what: Four readings of the ruling, taken as the lane built them (reversible): (1) the dispatch margin applies ON TOP of the floor - a haul from an ordered pool must beat the floor by the same margin it must beat home by (the floor acts as that pool's home price when it is higher); (2) several orders on one (corp, body, good): the HIGHEST floor binds; (3) a quantity cap limits only what is listed at home per tick, not what may be hauled; (4) REVERSED by the cold review (2026-10-07): a pool hauled empty must NOT close its order, or the haul then ships below the floor and the ruling breaks - a pool hauled from this tick counts as not empty. Floors almost never bind today (0.25-0.31x base, 3 of 782 surplus-ticks), so (1) and (2) rarely matter in play.

items.title: Decision taken on your behalf: spare supply stays a conservative estimate where several markets share one producer (BL-1233)
items.source: the BL-1233 (processors to inputs) round 2 re-review, 2026-10-08
items.what: The sized test's spare (input_reach.cpp reachable_supply) charges each consumer market min(its draw, the output of the markets that reach it), split among those markets by output. Where one producer is reached by several hungry consumers it can still be charged past its output (P2 making 10, reached by C, Q1, Q2 each drawing 10 -> spare 0, true 10). This only ever REFUSES a plant that could stand, never admits one that cannot; the exact answer needs a small max-flow per input. TAKEN: accepted as a conservative estimate, with a code comment naming it. Reversible; say if you want the exact (max-flow) reading.

items.title: Decision taken on your behalf: a nation's want for a good nobody holds yet is recorded at its capital market
items.source: the BL-1227 (idle mines) round 4 build and re-review
items.what: Your ruling: the space programme's / network upkeep's want counts as a bid "there", filled or not. When no pool or shelf anywhere holds the good, there is no "there" to read, so the build records the want at the nation's CAPITAL market. Effect: one such chain (propellant, spacecraft components) can start per nation, at its capital; once a plant exists the want follows the good. In play this took spacecraft-components plants from 0 to 22 on 5 seeds. TAKEN as built and written into AI_OPPONENT.md § 2B. Alternatives: every market of the nation (more starts, more idle risk), or the market nearest the nation's space infrastructure.

items.title: Decision taken on your behalf: an unpowered grid that no window can feed does not hold up the others (BL-1232)
items.source: the BL-1232 (power plants per grid) re-review, 2026-10-08
items.what: Your ruling: unpowered grids first - every short grid gets a plant before any gets a second. The re-review found that a short grid NO chartering centre's window can feed (no market centre on it, or its feeding markets outside every window) would hold the rule forever: every power firm narrowed to it, found no ground, and the core stopped getting plants. TAKEN: such a grid is dropped from the unpowered set for that centre, so an unreachable grid never holds up the others; if nothing unpowered is reachable, every short grid is served. Reversible: the strict reading (the rule holds even for an unreachable grid) starves the body's core.

items.title: Decision taken on your behalf: 'never cleared' is read from the market's current state, not a stored first-clear tick (BL-1217 D3b)
items.source: cold re-review of the BL-1217 D3 round 3 (a37f2099), sprint 50
items.what: Your ruling: the dial forecasts at base 'only on a market that has never cleared'; the build veto takes the same 'no clear yet: no signal' reading. Both now read market_has_cleared from fields only the clear writes (supply, demand, hauler_want) - fixing a real hole where a market spawned mid-step read as cleared. TAKEN: kept the state proxy. Gap: a market that HAS cleared but is wholly dead (no supply, demand or silenced want on any good) reads 'never cleared' again, so the veto gives no signal and the dial forecasts at base there - the old test had the same gap. Practically unreachable today (off-world markets get interbody demand; home markets carry people). Reversible: a set-once first-clear tick on the market would close it exactly, at the cost of a saved field (another save bump).

items.title: Decision taken on your behalf: a non-player roster corporation left with no holdings stays on legacy and no-budget worlds (BL-1217 D6)
items.source: the BL-1217 D5/D6 harness audit, sprint 50
items.what: Your rulings bound every processor by want and unplace a recipe-less processor whose default output is unwanted. On the LEGACY landscape apply (no budget, refused budget or no specialists) that leaves 1 non-player roster corporation with no holdings (2 in two cases); the budget path - every shipped campaign - removes the roster right after, and the player is never left holdless. TAKEN: leave the holdless corporation as is (it holds cash and a seat in the roster, acts on nothing). Reversible: remove a non-player roster corporation that ends generation with no holdings.

items.title: Sprint 51 write-up: five calls taken on Ben's behalf beyond the design form
items.source: the sprint 51 design write-up, 2026-10-08 (RENDERING.md, SELECTION.md, LENSES.md, PLANETARY.md; BL-1239..BL-1244)
items.what: The form settled the shape; writing it into the docs needed five smaller calls, each now in its owning doc and reversible there. (a) COMPANY LENS DEFAULT - no firm picked, so every firm's ground opens owned-grey: the player owns no company, so "the player only" has no counterpart (LENSES.md § Company lens). Alternative: every firm picked (the old look). (b) RIVAL ROWS IN THE PRODUCTION SECTION show type, count and owner; output and running state read "private", matching the rival building card (SELECTION.md). Alternative: running state public, since a working plant is observable. (c) SCAFFOLDING - "the art is static" has one exception, a construction site bakes as scaffolding, because start and completion are events rather than ticks and so cost no per-tick re-bake (RENDERING.md § Installations). (d) A FOURTH STACK adds nothing to the ground (the cluster caps at three), and a small settlement may vanish at the far page where the density dot stood; a scale >= 3 centre must still read as a city at every rung. (e) NEVER-MAGNIFY shifts every rung up one tier (13 px rung -> 24 px tier, top rung -> 192), and supersampling bakes the 192 tier at 384 px per hex - four times the bake pixels on the worker. BL-1244 measures bake time and memory before and after; if the 192 x 2 bake is too slow, the lever is to supersample only the tiers below it.

items.title: The player's nation has its budget scored by nation_ai, against NATIONS.md and AI_OPPONENT.md § 11
items.source: BL-1275 (nation research AI) lane report, confirmed by reading src/world/nation_ai.cpp:543 and nation_step.cpp:54

items.title: BL-1352 (one LP system): three readings taken so a march could draw the nation's pool
items.source: BL-1352 build, main session
items.what: The march now draws Logistic Points and claims ahead of production. Four readings the doc does not settle, each cheap to change. (1) WHOSE POOL - THE MOVER'S. A corporation's march draws its HOME NATION's points, a nation's garrison its own; never the pool of the ground it stands on. The first cut read the ground's nation and a cold review caught both consequences: a unit whose points ran out on unowned wilderness could never be granted again (a refusal moves nothing, so it re-fired for ever and the unit was stranded for good), and a unit invading another nation drew ITS VICTIM's pool, starving the defender's industry to fund the attack. LOGISTICS.md's 'Movement a player or rival DIRECTS' is the reading taken. The alternative - the ground's nation, with a stranding escape and a foreign-ground rule - is a real design and is Ben's if he wants it. (2) NO REACH TEST ON A MARCH - a unit draws its own nation's pool at full strength wherever it stands, because the off-network military reach is still 'military detail later' (LOGISTICS.md). (3) THE CLAIM IS GATHERED BEFORE THE BATTLE PHASE - the resolve runs at tick phase 4 and the march at phase 11, with battles at 10, so a unit killed in battle has already consumed its nation's points for that tick; the alternative is resolving the pool twice a tick. (4) THE EXCHANGE RATE IS UNCHANGED - one point admits one march-point of movement (infantry 1.0, cavalry 1.5 a tick) against a production need of 10 per unit of run, so a 50-unit army asks for ~60 points of a pool measured in the hundreds. Nothing measured says a soldier-tick and a unit of grain burden a nation equally; the old per-anchor rate (20/tick at every city) carried the same assumption.
items.why_it_matters: Reading 4 decides whether 'guns, butter and freight compete in one currency' is felt at all: at these numbers a march is a rounding error against production, which is the opposite of the campaign-starves-its-industry cost the doc describes. Reading 1 is the one that changes what a war looks like - who pays for an invasion's logistics. The 2040 spectator run is the measurement that should settle 4.
items.call: Accept the four, or name the one to move - most likely the march's weight (4), once the 2040 run shows what an army actually costs a nation.
items.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-23 (the sprint 55 close form): (1) the mover's own nation pays, as built. (4) the 1:1 exchange rate is kept as settled, not as a reading awaiting the 2040 measurement. Readings (2) and (3) stand as built.

items.title: BL-1346 (market attraction): the off-road leg's price, and what it costs to cross water
items.source: BL-1346 build + cold review, main session
items.what: MARKETS.md rules that catchment is logistics cost over pull, and LOGISTICS.md section 3b rules an off-road tile is priced by 'the off-road cost per tile times the number of 4-cardinal steps'. Two things the docs do not settle were decided in band. (1) THE PRICE: k_offroad_leg_per_tile = 3.0, taken from the Logistic Point model's own off-network step (lp_offnet_step) so the two off-road prices agree rather than drifting apart; it is dear against a plains road step of 1.0 before the tier discount, which is what keeps a market's edge following the road. (2) TERRAIN: the leg is multiplied by the tile's own traversal weight, so crossing a mountain or open water costs proportionally more than crossing a field. The doc says 'per tile' and is silent on terrain; a flat leg would price an unroaded island tile three steps across the sea exactly as a field three steps across a meadow, which a cold review flagged as the one place the walk ignores a domain every other cost walk in the tree respects.
items.why_it_matters: The leg decides how far a market's edge bulges past the end of its roads, and the terrain term decides whether islands and far coasts belong to the market across the water from them. Measured on seed 0 after the change: market_viability pooled G1 92.0 -> 90.1, G1t50 88.1 -> 86.3, G2 182.1 -> 185.0, all five gates still passing, and the same-nation fifth moves 279 of 31581 tiles.
items.call: Accept both, or name the price. The census and the gates are the instruments; the one reading most likely to want moving is the terrain multiplier on water.
items.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-23 (the sprint 55 close forms): keep 3.0 x terrain for market attraction, as built. The leg prices catchment only and moves no Logistic Points; off the networks, points supply units alone. Written into LOGISTICS.md section 3b.

items.title: BL-1311 (ground paint perf) builds the ground bake at /O2 in Debug: a new object library and CMake policy CMP0184
items.source: BL-1311 lane report (commit 3af45cdb); CMakeLists.txt
items.what: The four bake files (ground_bake, structure_stamps, route_paint, terrain_palette) now build as their own library at /O2 even in Debug, with runtime checks off; CMake policy CMP0184 is switched on so Debug runtime checks become a per-target property, and /RTC1 is stripped from the cached Debug flags for top-level targets (they keep the checks through the property). IO_OPTIMISE_GROUND_BAKE_IN_DEBUG=OFF restores single-stepping. Existing build trees rebuild once. This cut the Debug seat wait from 750 s to 12.7 s with byte-identical captures.
items.why_it_matters: It changes what the Debug build means for one subsystem (no runtime checks, not steppable by default) and touches every build tree; a build-system change is project-wide scope.
items.call: Keep (default ON), keep but default OFF, or revert to a plain Debug bake.
items.resolution: Ben: keep the /O2 ground-bake library in Debug, on by default (IO_OPTIMISE_GROUND_BAKE_IN_DEBUG=ON).

items.title: BL-1382 band scaling: f(s) = 1 + (s-1)/2 by anchor scale
items.source: PROVINCES.md § The normalising pass
items.what: Ben ruled the band (merge under 24, split over 100) and that it scales with the centre scale 1-5. The scaling form is mine: f(s) = 1 + (s-1)/2, so 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3 for scales 1-5 (village 24-100, scale-5 city 72-300). Chosen because the measured covered-land province mean by anchor scale runs s1 75, s2 88, s3 145 (a scale-3 about twice a scale-1).
items.why_it_matters: It sets how much larger a city province may be than a village one, and so how many splits a world takes.
items.call: Confirm, or name another scaling (e.g. linear in s, or the reach weight 60/s).
items.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-23 (the sprint 55 close form): f(s) = 1 + (s-1)/2, x1 to x3, as built.

items.title: No doc owns who holds a Logistic Points hub placed during generation; a broke major idles its hubs and starves its consumers
items.source: BL-1382 economy trace (seed 28), src/world/logistic_points.cpp seed_logistics_sources / place_hub, src/world/state_industry.cpp plan_state_funding
items.what: seed_logistics_sources gives every hub on a major's ground to the nation as state industry (NATIONS.md § State industry: transport is state industry; a losing building idles, never debt). A major leaving generation with treasury 0.0 idles all its hubs at tick 0, so its consumers get 0 Logistic Points and the loss reflex decommissions them. BL-1382's merges moved 181 consumers onto such a major on seed 28 (G1 96.8 -> 44.7). Present before BL-1382 at smaller scale (seeds 9, 32, 40). The seeding report also claims 100% coverage before the funding gate runs.
items.why_it_matters: Hub ownership at generation is a design rule no economy doc states; LOGISTICS.md says anyone may build one, NATIONS.md makes transport state industry.
items.call: A) a hub on a major that cannot fund it goes to the consumer's owner; B) no major leaves generation with a zero treasury; C) an unfunded state hub runs on upkeep goods; D) the landscape search scores LP supply. Asked in the session form 2026-10-18.
items.resolution: Ben: B — no major leaves generation on a zero treasury (Pass 7). Foundings keep a year (four ticks) of the state bill; the poorest realms earn more in the history until none closes empty. The LP coverage report reads the funding gate.

items.title: Tile Logistics section: Uses counts only the player's own buildings
items.source: BL-1354 (tile logistics section), built 2026-10-20
items.what: Ben asked for the points consumed by a tile. A rival building's point need is workforce x target, i.e. its run rate, which DISCOVERY.md keeps private. Taken on Ben's behalf: Uses counts the player's own buildings (god view: all), and the hover names how many rival buildings were left out. SELECTION.md records it.

items.title: Rail's fade past 20: kept at 8 (zero at 28), not the road's double-distance rule
items.source: BL-1360 (road tier extends reach), cold review finding 5
items.what: Your ruling gives rail 20 tiles and gives the zero-at-double fade to ROADS (Track 6/12, Road 8/16, Highway 10/20). Rail's fade was left at its existing 8, so a station 24 track steps down the line gets half strength and one at 28+ gets nothing. LOGISTICS.md says only '20 tiles' for rail.
items.why_it_matters: It decides whether a station 21-27 steps away is served at all. Today that is a fading partial, and the census moved little on it (rail sources unchanged: 69 / 0 / 185 on seeds 0 / 28 / 46).
items.call: a) keep fade 8: full to 20, zero at 28 (built); b) a hard edge: full to 20, nothing past it (fade 0); c) the road rule generalised: zero at 40 (fade 20).
items.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-23 (the sprint 55 close form): rail takes the road's rule - full to 20, zero at double, 40. Written into LOGISTICS.md; the constant change is work (lp_fade_length rail 8 -> 20).

items.title: Routing: does an isolated hub still add to the nation pool?
items.source: BL-1356 (routed requests), second cold review finding 3
items.what: As built, every running source adds its points to the one nation pool (your 'one nation pool' ruling), connected or not; routing only decides which requests may draw and in what order. So a hub with no chain to the capital delivers to nobody but still raises the pool every connected request draws from. LOGISTICS.md says such a hub 'supplies nothing', which reads as stricter.
items.why_it_matters: Decides whether an outlying hub is worthless until connected, or a pool top-up anywhere. Generation step 2 (pool sufficiency) places hubs for pool alone, so it leans on the as-built reading.
items.call: a) keep: every running source adds to the pool (built); b) only connected sources add to the pool.
items.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-21 (routing form): b) only connected sources add to the pool. Built in BL-1356: lp_source_row::connected; generation's pool hubs stand only where they join the chain.

items.title: Routing: does a road hub connect a station it covers, or only the reverse?
items.source: BL-1356 (routed requests), second cold review finding 2
items.what: The chain admits a source when ITS OWN reach touches the capital or a connected source's tile (your wording, built literally). A rail station's field holds only station tiles, so a station joins only through another connected station, or by standing on the capital or a connected source's tile. A connected road hub whose reach covers the station does NOT connect it. So a line between two provincial cities, neither linked by rail to a station at the capital, delivers nothing.
items.why_it_matters: Rail is the inter-market carrier; under the literal rule most generated lines may sit outside every chain. Not yet measured per line.
items.call: a) keep the literal one-way rule (built); b) either direction: a source joins if its reach touches the chain OR a connected source's reach touches it.
items.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-21 (routing form): b) a link counts in either direction. Built in BL-1356 (memo_chain); a connected road hub covering a station puts the line on the chain.

items.title: Routing: rival siting still buys one hub where a chain is needed (an AI grant question)
items.source: BL-1356 (routed requests), second cold review finding 1; AI_OPPONENT.md § 11
items.what: corp_ai prices an out-of-reach build at one hub and builds that hub on or beside the site. Under routing, a hub there counts only if it chains back to the capital, so on far ground the rival pays upkeep for a hub that never covers its site. The scorer's INPUT (lp_coverage_at) follows the new rule; its RESPONSE does not.
items.why_it_matters: Rivals will over-build isolated hubs on far ground. Teaching the scorer to lay a chain is new AI behaviour, so it is a grant for you to give or refuse, not an in-place fix.
items.call: a) leave the scorer as is and accept the waste; b) grant: the scorer prices and builds a chain to the capital; c) the scorer declines builds it cannot connect with one hub.
items.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-21 (routing form): b) granted - the scorer prices and builds the chain. Recorded in AI_OPPONENT.md section 11 'AI lays a hub chain to reach the capital'; the work is BL-1395 (AI_LAYS_HUB_CHAIN).

items.title: Rival hub chains on the player's nation's ground: builder or ground?
items.source: BL-1395 (rival lays a hub chain), cold review finding 4
items.what: Your grant excludes 'any chain for the player's nation or champion'. The 2026-10-15 grant's like wording is implemented as a BUILDER test (the player's corp and champion never source). Built conservatively: a rival building on the PLAYER's nation's ground keeps the old rule exactly - one hub on or beside the site, priced as one - and never lays a chain there. Elsewhere it lays the full chain.
items.why_it_matters: On the player's ground a rival's far site gets one hub that may not connect (so it covers nothing and adds nothing to the pool), while on every other nation's ground it gets a working chain. Reading the wording as builder-only would let rivals lay working chains on the player's ground too - hubs that also feed the player's pool.
items.call: a) keep (built): no rival chain on the player's ground, the old one-hub rule there; b) builder reading: a rival may lay a chain on any ground, the player's included; c) no rival sourcing on the player's ground at all.
items.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-23 (the sprint 55 close forms): stricter than either reading - a rival may build NOTHING on the player's nation's ground (AI_OPPONENT.md section 11, a narrowing). And a shipment needs the Logistic Points of its WHOLE route, from its market's centre to the market it trades with, international trades included (LOGISTICS.md, SUPPLY.md). Both are work, filed in the backlog.

items.title: Ports cross sea, not lakes
items.source: BL-1396 (port reach over water), cold review finding 7
items.what: Your rule says a port's points cross 'water'. Built as SEA only (ocean and coast), matching how placement already reads a coast: a lakeshore is not a coast, so a port cannot stand on one, and a sea port's points do not cross a lake to land on its shore.
items.why_it_matters: Decides whether a lake joined to the coast by a port reach counts as water the points travel over. Rare on generated worlds; no measured case.
items.call: a) sea only (built); b) any water, lakes included.
items.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-21: 'Ports should be able to cover lakes too.' b) any water: the sea walk crosses lakes and lands on their shores; a port still stands only on a sea coast. Built in BL-1396.

items.title: What a shipment's anchor draws against, now that the pool is the nation's
items.source: BL-1361 (a shipment draws points by cargo), as the handoff asked: decide and log
items.what: Built: the anchor is the SOURCE MARKET'S CENTRE TILE. A shipment draws one point a unit from what the march and production left in the pool of the nation whose ground that tile is; the centre's routed cover caps its share (a half-covered centre ships half of each cargo); a centre on nobody's ground, or one no connected source reaches, ships nothing; under a share rule the trader draws its own class's pot; space legs draw nothing. The rival Marketplace estimate reads the anchor's leftover again (its grant text never stopped saying so) and scales by the cover. Written into LOGISTICS.md section How a tile's points get to it.
items.why_it_matters: Trade now waits on logistics at its source. Measured (16-seed market_viability, haulage --far-trade) before -> after: convoys window E 868 -> 791, Y 909 -> 803; units E 7493 -> 6308, Y 7178 -> 5561; G1t50 89.8 -> 88.2 and G2 176.3 -> 158.8, every gate passing; per seed G1t50 under 85 on seeds 12 (79.4), 46 (81.6), 10 (81.8) and 32 (84.4). A market centre generation leaves uncovered ships nothing until somebody builds a source there - which BL-1367's lesser sources at market centres would answer.
items.call: a) keep (built); b) draw at the nearest connected source rather than the centre tile, so cover never caps; c) let an uncovered centre ship at a floor share.
items.known_limit: market_component::trade_lp_spare, which the rival estimate reads, is every class's pot together: under a share rule (only a seated player sets one) a rival on that ground may estimate on a pot its class cannot draw.
items.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-23 (the logistics funding form): keep the centre tile. a) as built.

items.title: 'The capital is the peak' read as: every capital covered at full strength
items.source: BL-1367 (where generation puts sources), re-read against routing as the handoff asked
items.what: Your 2026-10-18 rule says no tile of a nation may hold more points than its capital at generation. It was written for a field of points incident at a tile. Since BL-1356 a tile's points arrive as a SHARE of its request, at most all of it, so no tile can outrun a capital covered at full strength. Built: the check is that every capital is covered at full strength, which the state hub generation now stands on every capital guarantees. The census's old points-incident figures (cap_pts / max_pts) are still printed as report, and by that measure a rail station's tile still outruns most capitals.
items.why_it_matters: Decides whether the census gate is the routing reading (built; passes on all 16 seeds) or the field reading (fails wherever rail runs).
items.call: a) the routing reading (built); b) the field reading: points incident, rail included.
items.resolution: Ben, 2026-10-23 (the logistics funding form): the routing reading. a) as built.

items.title: Sprint 57 doc sweep: readings taken on your behalf re-subjecting ~60 docs to nations
items.source: sprint 57 doc sweep (four lanes, main session review)
items.what: Taken in band while re-subjecting the corpus to 'nations own everything'. ECONOMY: FINANCE drops the '<5% of a median firm's income' anchor and the [in debt] flag; glut clearing rests on idling (no building-exit rule); the tariff triggers on the convoy's OWNING nation; MARKETS' listed value retires with no replacement; generated Marketplaces may now land on the player's ground; opening stock falls back to the capital's market where it used the HQ's; POPULATION's labour share stays the share of building count; CONTRACTS keeps no live form between nations. GENERATION: CORPORATION_GENERATION retitled Industry Generation; a charter is a priced set of buildings owned by the centre's nation; per-firm capital no longer sizes opening stock; focus is kept per charter, region-derived; INDUSTRIALISATION's listed value sums building book value. Main session: 'no capital starts dark' stands, paid from the nation's whole treasury (LOGISTICS).
items.why_it_matters: Each is a faithful reading, but together they re-shape a lot of prose at once; any one you would rule differently is cheap to change before the code lanes build against it.

items.title: Too many majors: the poorest surplus major is DEMOTED to a minor, not folded into another
items.source: sprint 57 doc sweep, main session correction
items.what: The 2026-10-11 reconciliation folded the poorest major's SPECIALISTS into the richest major's champion; ground never moved. With no corporations there is nothing to move, so the faithful reading is a demotion: the poorest surplus major becomes a minor and keeps its ground and buildings, and the nation total is untouched. A lane had written it as a territorial fold, which would have cut the nation count by one outside the total's reconciliation; corrected in NATION_GENERATION.md and NATIONS.md § Own ground. BL-1404 (generation buys for nations) builds it.

items.title: Six questions the sweep could not settle once corporations retired
items.source: sprint 57 doc sweep
items.what: (1) EMBLEMS: PROFILE.md and ICONS.md now key the player's emblem by nation id, which sits against ICONS' own 'no nation flags' rule - keep a corporate-style emblem for the nation, or no emblem. (2) EMBARGO: what an embargo between nations gates, now there is no procurement between firms (RELATIONS.md open question 4). (3) DISCLOSURE: may the player read a rival nation's quarterly return or treasury (FINANCE.md § Disclosure; RELATIONS open question 5). (4) WORKS LEAN: INDUSTRIALISATION's Private Works vs State Arsenal fork has no subject - derive it some other way, or retire it. (5) INDUSTRIAL FOCUS: whether a nation's build scorer keeps a focus weight (AI_OPPONENT ~789) or it retires with the specialist. (6) INDUSTRY LENS: re-subjected to 'plants of nations other than the player's' - keep, or retire.

items.recommendation: (1) no emblem until designed; (2) an embargo bars a nation's goods from entering your markets; (3) a rival's treasury is private, its GDP public; (4) retire; (5) keep focus as the nation's economic_focus; (6) keep.

items.title: BL-1403 (nation money flows): the tax rates now bite on wages, and a nation's import duty is capped at its treasury
items.source: BL-1403 build, main session
items.what: (1) WAGE TAX RATES: the tier rates I..V (0 / 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 %) were calibrated as shares of a firm's operating PROFIT; under your ruling they are now shares of the WAGES a nation pays, which is a much larger base, so tier V returns a fifth of the whole wage bill. Kept unchanged in band; the post-fold measurement will say whether the tiers still read as a trade-off against Discontent. (2) DUTY CAP: a nation never runs into debt, so when a nation (not a corporation) owes import duty on goods entering a foreign market, the duty is capped at what its treasury holds; the cargo still lands. The alternative is refusing the shipment at dispatch when the importer cannot pay, which is a larger change to the trade pass.
items.why_it_matters: (1) decides whether a high tax tier is a strong lever or a free one; (2) decides whether a broke nation can keep importing.

items.title: BL-1402 (fold to ground): market_viability's G2/G3 re-pointed, and the seat's clean slate now covers its whole nation
items.source: BL-1402 build + cold review, main session
items.what: (1) G2 (field income) summed each corporation's filed income; after the fold every corporation earns nothing and G2 read 0.0. It now adds each nation's state-ledger income (its buildings' sales) - the same 'whole field's sales' quantity. (2) G3 (firms alive at the last tick / at the handoff) has no subject on a folded world. Re-pointed to BUILDINGS alive at the last tick / at the handoff, target unchanged at 70% - the closest question ('does the handoff economy survive the play'); the alternative of nations alive is vacuous (a nation only dies by conquest). (3) Firm exit is inert on a folded world: it would erase the empty champion records the major/minor reading still keys on until BL-1407. (4) BL-1206's seat clean slate (the seat's unfinished settle builds cancelled and refunded) now cancels the seat NATION's unfinished builds, its own AI's settle sites included - the ruling re-subjected to 'the seat is the nation'. (5) A nation's trade reserve is not carried by the fold and a nation cannot set one until BL-1407 saves the field (generation leaves every reserve at 0).
items.why_it_matters: (1)-(2) change what two merge gates measure; (4) decides how much construction the player's nation opens without.

items.title: After the fold, nations' treasuries fall during play, and on seed 46 the majors stop building
items.source: BL-1402 gate, main session
items.what: On the folded world (BL-1402), seed 46's 4 majors place NO production building in 40 seated ticks (seeds 0 and 28 still pass: 3/5 and 1/1). Diagnosed 2026-10-24 with nation_ai_builds' new diagnostic lines: every extraction candidate is refused before selection - placement (60-210 per major), construction materials not obtainable (30-110), net <= 0 and glut vetoes - and the majors decide only dials; their treasuries are far above the floor (e.g. 8549 vs 312) but FALLING (27407 -> 8549 over the window for nation 47763). A reading of a thin, glutted economy, not a scorer defect; the row is left failing rather than weakened. Owned by BL-1409. market_viability FULL on the folded world still passes every gate: G1 92.9, G1t50 85.4 (target 85), G1b 4.6, G2 95.3, G3 100.0 (buildings alive, NR-1068). BL-1403 (tax from wages, no levy) is not applied yet; its wage tax returns 10% of wages at tier III, which slows the fall.
items.why_it_matters: A nation that pays every wage and input from one treasury, and whose treasury drains, idles its buildings one by one under the never-debt rule - the folded economy's long-run health is the question BL-1409 measures.

items.title: NOVEL WORK (BL-1406): a verify-only staging call verify.fold_world, seven retired verify scripts deleted, and a golden blessed under a retired lens
items.source: BL-1406 lane (UI and protocol as nation)
items.what: (1) A new verify-only STAGING call, verify.fold_world, runs fold_to_ground on the --verify world (whose builder does not go through finish_campaign_world), and verify.buildings() lists nation buildings once folded. The standing rules record dated scoped exceptions for what the verify API may reveal or stage (road_admits, find_water_crossing, stage_road); this is a fifth of that family, raised here rather than assumed. (2) Seven verify scripts for retired surfaces (Corporation / Company lenses, acquisitions, company ledger, stance table) were deleted and ~15 re-pointed to the Nations lens; .claude/skills/verifier-visual/SKILL.md still names the deleted ones - a skill edit, which is yours to approve. (3) The icon_silhouettes_overview golden was blessed with the retired Corporation lens on screen, so it now differs; the golden policy says no bulk re-bless and --bless never creates - a single re-bless needs your go (BL-1408).
items.why_it_matters: (1) widens what verify scripts may do to the world; (2) and (3) are your gates on skills and goldens.
items.recommendation: (1) grant, verify-only and behind --verify like its siblings; (2) approve trimming the deleted names from SKILL.md; (3) re-bless the one golden at BL-1408.

items.title: BL-1407 consequences: unit upkeep now runs only as the garrison budget claim, the nation scorer does not hire, and two smaller readings
items.source: BL-1407 lane + main session
items.what: (1) UNIT UPKEEP: the credits+goods+supply-decay vector (run_unit_upkeep) only ever ran for CORPORATION units; with corporations gone every unit takes the garrison branch, whose upkeep is a military_research budget-line claim (MILITARY.md § Nation garrisons) - so the per-unit vector no longer runs anywhere. That is MILITARY.md's model for a nation's units, applied to all of them. (2) HIRE: the scorer's corporation hire/base branch is left OFF for nations - a nation raises force through the muster (MILITARY.md), and opening the corporation hire path too would give it two. The 2026-10-23 grant named hiring among the carried-over decisions, so this is a narrowing. (3) THE SCORER'S TRADE, MARKETPLACE AND SURVEY BRANCHES are dead after the delete (they were corporation-only), so no AI nation pins a trade, builds a Marketplace or surveys; AUTO trade still runs. Re-opening them under the grant (BL-1402 T8, parked as docs/development/drafts/bl-1402-t8-nation-ai-trade.patch) was measured: market_viability FULL G1t50 85.2 -> 84.0 (FAILS the 85 target), G2 94.1 -> 96.9, G1b 4.6 -> 4.9; with manual pins off but Marketplace and surveys on, G1t50 84.6 (still fails) and G1b 5.0. Left OFF so the gates pass; YOUR CALL: re-open (and accept or re-target the gate), or keep off until BL-1409 explains how a whole-economy nation trades against its own plants. (4) A nation's quarterly return counts the wage tax as income; the seat card's trailing net still reads 0 though nations now file returns.
items.why_it_matters: (1) and (2) decide what a nation's army costs it and how it grows one; (3) restores AI trade, which otherwise stopped entirely.
items.recommendation: Keep it off and fold the question into BL-1409, whose measurement (treasury trajectory and seed 46) is the same question of how a nation that owns every plant spends.

items.title: Network upkeep bills 2-4x the world's stone and timber, so trade buildings starve and auto trade stops by tick 4
items.source: Ben's live click (trade from the start) + diagnosis lane, 2026-10-24
items.what: Ben asked for Marketplaces and automatic trade from the start. Generation places them (17 Marketplaces, 11 Ports on seed 0). Two causes stopped the trade: (1) FIXED - the fold discarded the opening stock (c404a607), so shelves opened empty; now 81 then 36 auto shipments go out on ticks 2-3. (2) OPEN - network upkeep (BL-643, the logistics_maintenance line; scripts/economy.lua network_upkeep) bills ~2383 stone and ~1191 timber a tick on seed 0 (3402 highway + 2480 road edges, 130 hubs; seed 1 3065/1532, seed 28 1356/678, seed 46 2346/1173) against ~640 stone / ~580 timber dug. Each nation buys from the largest shelf anywhere, after the clear, so the trade buildings' own upkeep (coal 0.25 / timber 0.15 / stone 0.15 a Marketplace) finds empty shelves and they make no trade points. The fold made it bite: the firms' cash now sits in treasuries, so the maintenance line can afford the whole bill (before, timber drew 5-46 a tick; now 100-1043). It was already partly true before the sprint: pre-fold seed 0 also starved stone by tick 4 and haulage read 0 convoys there - the old 868 came from seeds 1 and 2. Not the cause: no producer idled, Logistic Points fully granted, network code unchanged.
items.why_it_matters: Trade - one of the two pillars - stops in the first year on every measured seed, and the logistics network looks broken while the money flows elsewhere.
options: A) Re-rate network upkeep down to what the world produces (a constant retune: the 'tens per quarter' figure holds per nation but sums to 2-4x supply).
B) A nation buys its network upkeep only from its OWN markets, not the largest shelf in the world (a draw rule).
C) Serve trade-building upkeep before network upkeep (an order of service).
D) Accept it: trade stops until supply catches up.
items.recommendation: A and B together: the rate is an authored first cut ('retune by playtest'), and buying repairs from the far side of the world is the part that drains every trade shelf.
